_README: Scenario overrides. `supplyModel` selects an entry of params.supplyModels. `prices` are OUR retail prices in PLN. `overrides` deep-merges into params, so a scenario can change any input. Conservative must be genuinely pessimistic — if it looks comfortable, it is not conservative.
_pricingBasis: All three price ladders sit inside the VERIFIED Polish accessible-speciality band of 120-190 PLN/kg (CMP-46) and respect the two verified market regularities: 1 kg undercuts 250 g by 9-28% per kg, and the 149 PLN free-delivery threshold forces the basket towards 1 kg or three bags.

conservative._stance: The verified private-label cost is real and does not improve. We have no brand, so we price at the LOW end of accessible speciality to get a first order. Repeat behaviour matches the discouraging Polish loyalty evidence. Founder labour is costed at a real rate.

base._stance: A negotiated contract-roasting price somewhat better than the single public quote, priced at the middle of accessible speciality, ordinary repeat behaviour, founder labour not charged (cash view).

costPerKgRoastedGross.src: ASSUMPTION(A1) — NOT VERIFIED. Assumes a quote ~11% better than the one public figure.

optimistic._stance: Good negotiated supply, priced at the upper end of accessible speciality, strong repeat. A CEILING, not a plan.

costPerKgRoastedGross.src: ASSUMPTION(A1) — NOT VERIFIED. Assumes volume terms a startup has no history to justify.

resale._stance: Sanity check on Route B — reselling someone else's brand. Cost is DERIVED, not public, so this scenario is illustrative only. Included because it shows whether resale is even worth quoting for.

baseVatRegistered._stance: Identical to base, except the company registers for VAT voluntarily. Isolates ONE variable: the B2B price handicap a non-VAT payer carries (REG-10). B2C rows are unchanged and can be ignored here.

conservativeVatRegistered._stance: The VERIFIED cost of 124 PLN/kg, founder labour charged, but VAT-registered. The honest worst case for a B2B-led plan.
